gaps.quote: every power of $\omega_t$ is an isometry
gaps.note: The page never says which norm on R_r is meant (the paper, line 2779-2784, uses the max of coefficient moduli, under which multiplication by y^a permutes coefficients and flips signs). Without it the reader cannot check that powers of omega_t are isometries, that averaging gives contractions, or that H_0 and J_E are a contraction and an isometry.

gaps.quote: since the additive group of $\mathcal R_r$ has no two-torsion (cited)
gaps.note: Two-torsion is abstract-algebra vocabulary the reader has not been taught, and the page does not explain it. The needed fact is that S=-S forces S=0 because 2S=0 and 2 is invertible on complex coefficient vectors; the page never says this.

gaps.term: named slots and the order of frequency bits
gaps.quote: After all $a$ rounds the named slots from high to low hold the frequency bits from low to high
gaps.note: Slots and address bits are never introduced on this page, and the induction over rounds (paper lines 2846-2862) that shows each round writes the next-lowest frequency bit into the high slots is not given. The reader cannot check this claim, which the bit-reversal and B_t rest on.

Both reverse operators composed with B_tF_t^- give I/t, but that equates them only if B_tF_t^- is invertible. The paper (line 2880-2881) states this hypothesis ('The forward procedure is invertible, so these two reverse operators agree'). The page omits it and never says the forward procedure is invertible.

gaps.quote: $k_i$ the index encoded by its unprocessed slots
gaps.note: The page does not say how k_i is read off from the address bits, nor that 0<=k_i<u_i/2, nor why the combined exponent is that sum. The formula for E is given without derivation and relies on the undefined slot encoding.
